exEn: Where did you put my things?
note: The plural saker often means 'stuff'. Also 'matter': Det är en annan sak (That's another matter).

exEn: Wait, I forgot one thing!
note: Very common in speech; sak is more neutral. Grejen är att … = The thing is …

exEn: What a great idea!
note: Stressed on the é. Det är ingen idé = There's no point.

exEn: Thanks, that was a nice thought.
note: The final -e drops before the endings: tanken, tankar.

ex: Min {dröm} är att bo vid havet.
exEn: My dream is to live by the sea.
note: The m doubles before an ending: drömmen, drömmar.

exEn: Do you have any plans for the weekend?
note: Careful: ett plan is a plane (flygplan) or a floor/level in a building (plan 3).

ex: Finns det någon {anledning} att oroa sig?
exEn: Is there any reason to worry?
note: av den anledningen = for that reason

exEn: The police don't know the cause of the fire.
note: orsaken till något = the cause of something. Ingen orsak! = Don't mention it!

exEn: We have a problem with the car.
note: An ett-word with no plural ending: ett problem, två problem.

exEn: We have to find a solution.
Everyone makes mistakes.
note: av misstag = by mistake. In everyday speech Swedes also say fel: Det var mitt fel (It was my fault).

exEn: In that case, I'll stay home.
note: i så fall = in that case; i alla fall = anyway, at least. It can also mean 'a fall'.

ex: Det är en svår {situation} för alla.
exEn: It's a difficult situation for everyone.
note: -tion is pronounced 'shoon' and carries the stress.

ex: Det här är en stor {möjlighet} för mig.
exEn: This is a big opportunity for me.
Give me one more chance!
note: A French loan: ch is the sj-sound, and the n usually sounds like ng.

exEn: I'm busy at the moment.
note: för tillfället = at the moment; vid tillfälle = when you get a chance.

ex: Det finns en {risk} att vi missar tåget.
exEn: There's a risk that we'll miss the train.
We were lucky with the weather.
note: ha tur = to be lucky; otur = bad luck. Det är din tur = It's your turn.

exEn: What's the difference between them?
note: sk before i is the sj-sound. Det gör ingen skillnad = It makes no difference.

ex: Det finns många {likheter} mellan svenska och norska.
exEn: There are many similarities between Swedish and Norwegian.
note: likheter och skillnader = similarities and differences

exEn: Can you give an example?
note: till exempel (t.ex.) = for example. The last e drops: exemplet, exemplen.

ex: Den första {delen} av filmen var bäst.
exEn: The first part of the movie was the best.
note: en del also means 'some': en del människor (some people).

exEn: What type of music do you like?
note: In casual speech typ also means 'like, sort of': Det tar typ en timme.

exEn: This kind is cheaper.
note: 'A kind of' is en sorts or ett slags: ett slags bröd.

ex: Det finns inget bättre {sätt} att lära sig.
exEn: There's no better way to learn.
note: på det sättet = that way; på något sätt = somehow. A way you walk or drive is en väg.

exEn: We're still waiting for the result.
What's the purpose of the meeting?
note: i syfte att = with the aim of (formal)

exEn: In the beginning it was hard.
note: Same form with and without 'the': i början av maj (at the beginning of May), en bra början (a good start).

exEn: Put the table in the middle of the room.
note: Mostly used as mitten: i mitten av juni (in the middle of June). Not to be confused with mitt (my).

exEn: The movie had a happy ending.
note: i slutet av maj = at the end of May. Also an adjective: Mjölken är slut (We're out of milk).

exEn: What do you want to do in the future?
That's a thing of the past.
note: Always with det. 'He has a past' is Han har ett förflutet.

ex: Det blir en stor {förändring} för barnen.
exEn: It will be a big change for the kids.
note: A small edit or correction is en ändring: en ändring i schemat (a change to the schedule).

exEn: It was a difficult decision.
note: fatta ett beslut = to make a decision

exEn: That was a good try!
note: The verb is försöka (to try).

exEn: You have to follow the rules.
note: The e of -el drops before an ending: regeln, regler. som regel = as a rule, usually.

exEn: Is everything all right?
note: i ordning = in order, OK: Det är i ordning (That's fine). An order in a shop or restaurant is en beställning.

exEn: It's your responsibility.
note: No plural. ta ansvar för = to take responsibility for; ansvarig = responsible.

exEn: He has a lot of power in the company.
note: Power over people. Physical strength is styrka; electric power is el or ström.

exEn: What are your strengths?
note: A classic job interview question, often followed by: Och dina svagheter?

exEn: Chocolate is my biggest weakness.

ex: Det finns ett stort {behov} av lärare.
exEn: There's a great need for teachers.
note: vid behov = when needed. The verb is behöva (to need).

exEn: She has a good knowledge of Swedish.
note: Often plural for knowledge of a subject: kunskaper i engelska.

ex: Jag har ett dåligt {minne} för namn.
exEn: I have a bad memory for names.
note: Both the ability (ett bra minne) and something remembered (fina minnen).

exEn: Tell the truth!
note: säga sanningen and tala sanning (no article) both mean 'to tell the truth'.

exEn: That's a lie!
note: gn sounds like ngn: 'löngn'. The verb is ljuga (to lie).

exEn: In reality, it's harder.
note: i verkligheten = in reality, in real life

exEn: Smoking is a bad habit.
note: av gammal vana = out of habit; van vid = used to

exEn: Let's keep in touch!
note: ta kontakt med = to get in touch with. Also an electric plug or socket.

ex: Jag har en bra {relation} till min chef.
exEn: I have a good relationship with my boss.
note: Note the preposition: en relation till någon.

ex: De har haft ett {förhållande} i två år.
exEn: They've been in a relationship for two years.
note: i förhållande till = in relation to; the plural förhållanden often means 'conditions'.

exEn: The word has two meanings.
note: Det har ingen betydelse = It doesn't matter. The verb is betyda (to mean).

exEn: The house has increased in value.
The food is of high quality.
note: Also spelled kvalité, pronounced without the final t.

ex: Vilken {nivå} är du på i svenska?
exEn: What level are you at in Swedish?
He drinks huge amounts of coffee.
note: For things you count, use antal: ett stort antal bilar (a large number of cars).

exEn: The number of tourists increases every year.
note: How many there are. A phone number is ett nummer; a digit is en siffra.

ex: En stor {fördel} är att det är nära.
exEn: A big advantage is that it's close by.
The downside is that it's expensive.
note: fördelar och nackdelar = pros and cons
